arxiv-2101-11936.title: Photonic heat rectification in a coupled qubits system
arxiv-2101-11936.creator: A. Iorio, E. Strambini, G. Haack, M. Campisi, F. Giazotto
arxiv-2101-11936.description: Abstract We theoretically investigate a quantum heat diode based on two interacting flux qubits coupled to two heat baths. Rectification of heat currents is achieved by asymmetrically coupling the qubits to the reservoirs modelled as dissipative R ​ L ​ C RLC resonators.

arxiv-2112-00237.title: DECi-hertz Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory: Forecast constraints on the cosmic curvature with LSST strong lenses
arxiv-2112-00237.creator: Shuo Cao, Tonghua Liu, Marek Biesiada, Yuting Liu, Wuzheng Guo, Zong-Hong Zhu
arxiv-2112-00237.description: Abstract In this paper, we aim at using the DECi-hertz Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory (DECIGO), a future Japanese space gravitational-wave antenna sensitive to frequency range between LISA and ground-based detectors, to provide gravitational-wave constraints on the cosmic curvature at z ∼ 5 z\sim 5 .

arxiv-2304-04670.title: Let’s Stop Building at the Feet of Giants: Recovering unavailable Requirements Quality Artifacts
arxiv-2304-04670.creator: Julian Frattini, Lloyd Montgomery, Davide Fucci, Jannik Fischbach, Michael Unterkalmsteiner, Daniel Mendez
arxiv-2304-04670.description: Abstract Requirements quality literature abounds with publications presenting artifacts, such as data sets and tools. However, recent systematic studies show that more than 80% of these artifacts have become unavailable or were never made public, limiting reproducibility and reusability. In this work, we report on an attempt to recover those artifacts.

arxiv-2308-16134.title: Neutrino constraints on inelastic dark matter captured in the Sun
arxiv-2308-16134.creator: Ina Sarcevic ID
arxiv-2308-16134.description: Abstract The flux of neutrinos from annihilation of gravitationally captured dark matter in the Sun has significant constraints from direct-detection experiments. However, these constraints are relaxed for inelastic dark matter as inelastic dark matter interactions generate less energetic nuclear recoils compared to elastic dark matter interactions.

arxiv-2309-15673.title: Kähler–Yang–Mills Equations and Vortices This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Differential Geometry Inspired by Mathematical Physics in honor of Jean-Pierre Bourguignon for his 75th birthday. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Bourguignon.html
arxiv-2309-15673.creator: Oscar GARCÍA-PRADA
arxiv-2309-15673.description: Abstract The Kähler–Yang–Mills equations are coupled equations for a Kähler metric on a compact complex manifold and a connection on a complex vector bundle over it. After briefly reviewing the main aspects of the geometry of the Kähler–Yang–Mills equations, we consider dimensional reductions of the equations related to vortices — solutions to certain Yang–Mills–Higgs equations.

arxiv-2311-06353.title: Effective 2HDM Yukawa Interactions and a Strong First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition
arxiv-2311-06353.creator: Anisha, Duarte Azevedo, Lisa Biermann, Christoph Englert, and Margarete Mühlleitner
arxiv-2311-06353.description: Abstract The top quark as the heaviest particle in the Standard Model (SM) defines an important mass scale for Higgs physics and the electroweak scale itself. It is therefore a well-motivated degree of freedom which could reveal the presence of new interactions beyond the SM.

arxiv-2409-17368.title: EfiMon: A Process Analyser for Granular Power Consumption Prediction
arxiv-2409-17368.creator: Luis G. León-Vega, Niccolò Tosato, Stefano Cozzini
arxiv-2409-17368.description: Abstract High-performance computing (HPC) and supercomputing are critical in Artificial Intelligence (AI) research, development, and deployment. The extensive use of supercomputers for training complex AI models, which can take from days to months, raises significant concerns about energy consumption and carbon emissions.

arxiv-2505-09968.title: Stability and Bifurcation Analysis of a Phytoplankton-Zooplankton Model with Linear Functional Responses
arxiv-2505-09968.creator: S.K. Shoyimardonov
arxiv-2505-09968.description: Abstract . In this paper, the dynamics of a phytoplankton-zooplankton system with linear functional responses are examined. For the continuous-time model, the global asymptotic stability of the fixed points is demonstrated by constructing Lyapunov functions. For the discrete version of the model, both local and global dynamics are investigated using LaSalle’s Invariance Principle.

arxiv-2508-20883.title: Lattice Random Walk Discretisations of Stochastic Differential Equations
arxiv-2508-20883.creator: Samuel Duffield, Maxwell Aifer, Denis Melanson, Zach Belateche, Patrick J. Coles
arxiv-2508-20883.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Samuel Duffield, Maxwell Aifer, Denis Melanson, Zach Belateche, Patrick J. Coles. We introduce a lattice random walk discretisation scheme for stochastic differential equations (SDEs) that samples binary or ternary increments at each step, suppressing complex drift and diffusion computations to simple 1 or 2 bit random values.

europmc-pmc5346598.creator: McGowan JV, Chung R, Maulik A, Piotrowska I, Walker JM, Yellon DM.
europmc-pmc5346598.description: Anthracycline chemotherapy maintains a prominent role in treating many forms of cancer. Cardiotoxic side effects limit their dosing and improved cancer outcomes expose the cancer survivor to increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. The basic mechanisms of cardiotoxicity

pmc-10687212.title: Influence of PODE1 additive into ethanol-gasoline blends (E10) on fuel properties and phase stability
pmc-10687212.creator: Omar I. Awad, Bo Zhou, Zhenbin Chen, Kumaran Kadirgama, M.N. Mohammed, D. Ramasamy
pmc-10687212.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Polyoxymethylene dimethyl ethers (PODEn, n = 1–8) as an oxygenated fuel are a promising alternative fuel with a high oxygen concentration, a low C:H ratio, and no C–C bonds in their chemical structure. This could lead to smoke-free combustion. In this study, we chose to focus on PODE1 because of its lower cetane number, which makes it more suitable for use in spark ignition (SI) engines. However, its lower boiling point and octane number remain challenges.

pmc-11437623.title: Nursing perception towards the impact of JCI accreditation on the quality of care in a university hospital in Palestine: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11437623.creator: Loai M Zabin, Baraa F Shayeb, Amani A Abu Kishek, Mohammed Hayek
pmc-11437623.description: BackgroundThis study investigates nursing staff perceptions regarding the impact of Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation on the quality of care within a university hospital in Palestine. The research specifically examines how the accreditation process influences nursing practices, patient results, and overall healthcare quality in a challenging environment marked by unique operational and external pressures.

pmc-11503843.title: Characterizing Hematological Changes Following Repeated Exposure to Non-Targeted Low-Dose Ionizing Radiation in Prostate Cancer Patients
pmc-11503843.creator: Allison E Kennedy, Ian S Dayes, Sameer Parpia, Douglas R Boreham, Dawn M E Bowdish
pmc-11503843.description: The duration and magnitude of haematological changes following non-targeted low-dose radiation have not been well explored. We previously reported that low-dose radiation (150 mGy 2x/week for 5 consecutive weeks) was well tolerated by participants (n = 15) with minimal toxicities and no changes in quality of life.

pmc-11514270.title: IRF1-mediated upregulation of PARP12 promotes cartilage degradation by inhibiting PINK1/Parkin dependent mitophagy through ISG15 attenuating ubiquitylation and SUMOylation of MFN1/2
pmc-11514270.creator: Zengfa Deng, Dianbo Long, Changzhao Li, Hailong Liu, Wei Li, Yanlin Zhong, Xiaolin Mo, Ruiyun Li, Zibo Yang, Yan Kang, Guping Mao
pmc-11514270.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is an age-related cartilage-degenerating joint disease. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been reported to promote the development of OA. Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase family member 12 (PARP12) is a key regulator of mitochondrial function, protein translation, and inflammation. However, the role of PARP12 in OA-based cartilage degradation and the underlying mechanisms are relatively unknown.

pmc-11656970.title: Data mining in FAERS: association of newer-generation H1-antihistamines with nervous system disorders
pmc-11656970.creator: Weiping Hu, Hailong Li, Linan Zeng, Jing Gan, Chenghong Feng, Li Chen, Lingli Zhang
pmc-11656970.description: BackgroundH1-antihistamines are widely used to treat symptoms depending on histamine release in a variety of conditions. However, neurological adverse events have been reported in post-marketing surveillance studies and there are limited literatures comparing the neurological disorders associated with newer-generation H1-antihistamines from real-world datasets.

pmc-12656348.title: Genetic Divergence of H1N1pdm09 in Saudi Arabia: Unveiling a Novel N-Glycosylation Site and Its Role in Vaccine Mismatch
pmc-12656348.creator: Shatha Ata Abdulgader, Abdulhadi M Abdulwahed, Abdulaziz M Almuqrin, Ibrahim M Aziz, Noorah A Alkubaisi, Reem M Aljowaie, Mohamed A Farrag, Abdulkarim F Alhetheel, Adel A Abdulmanea, Fatimah N Alanazi, Asma N Alsaleh, Fahad N Almajhdi, Irina Kiseleva
pmc-12656348.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Influenza A virus undergoes continuous antigenic drift, necessitating annual vaccine reformulation. Saudi Arabia faces unique epidemiological challenges owing to mass gatherings during religious pilgrimages and the dynamic movement of foreign workers. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity of hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) genes of influenza A viruses circulating in Riyadh and to assess their match with vaccine strains during the 2024–2025 period. Methods: Nasopharyngeal samples (n = 363) were collected from patients presenting with influenza-like illness.

pmc-12866077.title: Shared muscle synergies between running and physical performance tests
pmc-12866077.creator: Hiroki Saito, Ayu Yamano, Nanae Suzuki, Kazuya Matsushita, Hikaru Yokoyama, Atsushi Sasaki, Tatsuya Takahashi, Sakiko Ito, Kimitaka Nakazawa
pmc-12866077.description: BackgroundUnderstanding whether commonly used physical performance test (PPT)-related tasks replicate the neuromechanical characteristics of running is essential for informing return-to-running (RTR) decisions. PPTs are frequently used in rehabilitation, yet their ability to reflect the neuromuscular demands of running has not been fully established.

pmc-13066339.title: Residential segregation and late-stage colorectal cancer in the United States: a population-based study of 1.2 million adults
pmc-13066339.creator: Eduardo J Santiago-Rodríguez, Justin S White, Zinzi D Bailey, Isabel E Allen, Robert A Hiatt, Salma Shariff-Marco
pmc-13066339.description: We examined the association between residential segregation and late-stage colorectal cancer (CRC) in the United States. The restricted-use United States Cancer Statistics database was used to identify all CRC cases diagnosed during 2009 to 2017. Late-stage CRC was determined according to the presence of distant involvement of the tumor at diagnosis.

pmc-13081299.title: The predictive value of tidal volume challenge-induced hemodynamic changes for fluid responsiveness in patients undergoing thoracoscopic surgery with one-lung ventilation: a prospective observational study
pmc-13081299.creator: Yong Zhan, Qi-quan Zhang, Xiao-qiang Wang, Hao Yuan, Jun-qing Li
pmc-13081299.description: BackgroundVideo-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) relies on one-lung ventilation (OLV) to achieve optimal surgical conditions. However, the lung protective ventilation strategies commonly employed during OLV diminish the accuracy of traditional dynamic parameters in predicting fluid responsiveness. The tidal volume challenge (TVC) has been proposed to overcome this limitation, yet its effectiveness in OLV patients remains to be validated.

pmc-13643000.title: Blood Lipid Levels and Intraocular Pressure in a Japanese Population: the JPHC-NEXT Eye Study
pmc-13643000.creator: Maho Sato, Akiko Hanyuda, Kazumasa Yamagishi, Kenya Yuki, Miki Uchino, Yoko Ozawa, Mariko Sasaki, Kazuo Tsubota, Kazuno Negishi, Norie Sawada, Shoichiro Tsugane, Hiroyasu Iso
pmc-13643000.description: Aim: Although growing epidemiological evidence suggests that metabolic risk factors may influence the intraocular pressure (IOP), the specific effects of individual lipid components on IOP regulation remain unclear. In this study, we examined the associations between the serum lipid profiles, individually and in combination, and IOP among 6,786 ophthalmologically healthy adults aged ≥ 40 years residing in Chikusei City, Japan.

pmc-13675463.title: Bibliometric mapping of research trends and publication growth in cancer sonodynamic therapy from 2001 to 2025
pmc-13675463.creator: Xiaoting Wang, Bo Zhang, Ke Yang, Peitong Deng
pmc-13675463.description: BackgroundSonodynamic therapy (SDT) is increasingly investigated for cancer treatment. This study aimed to characterize the knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and publication trajectory of cancer SDT research.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from January 1, 2001, to December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) on January 16, 2026. CiteSpace 6.4.R1 and VOSviewer 1.6.

uslaw-usc-t31-s5329.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s5329.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 53 (Monetary Transactions); Subchapter II (Records And Reports On Monetary Instruments Transactions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary shall— (1) publish all written rulings interpreting this subchapter; and (2) annually issue a staff commentary on the regulations issued under this subchapter.
